rows.question: My Limited Edition Beta copy of Lightning Bolt reads "Lightning Bolt does 3 damage to one target.". What does the card actually do now?
rows.answer:
Question type: printedVsOracle
Verdict: Your Limited Edition Beta printed wording is overridden — the card now reads "Lightning Bolt deals 3 damage to any target."
Missing: None
Why: Since your card is a Limited Edition Beta printing, the printed wording "one target" no longer describes the card's function. Under CR 108.1 you determine a card's wording from the Oracle card reference, so the current Oracle text is what governs, and it widened the target from "one target" to "any target," which adds planeswalkers and battles. A verified adjudication case exists for exactly this question and reaches the same result.
Governing authority: Current Oracle text (card "Lightning Bolt", current as of 2026-09-18), under CR 108.1.
Quote (current Oracle text): Lightning Bolt deals 3 damage to any target.
Quote (printed text, Limited Edition Beta, collector no. 162): Lightning Bolt does 3 damage to one target.
Quote (CR 108.1): Use the Oracle card reference when determining a card's wording. A card's Oracle text can be found using the Gatherer card database at Gatherer.Wizards.com.
Quote (reviewed decision, case.pvo-LEB-Lightning-Bolt, expected verdict): Current Oracle text governs under CR 108.1: "Lightning Bolt deals 3 damage to any target." The answer must reproduce this text completely and name the printing it overrules.
Rules: 108.1
Conflict: The Limited Edition Beta printed wording ("one target") conflicts with the current Oracle text ("any target"); CR 108.1 makes the Oracle wording govern. The recorded text similarity between the two is 0.600 and the difference is classified "functional," i.e. the wording change did alter how the card works.
Sources: card.4457ed35-7c10-48c8-9776-456485fdf070, printing.b5d3dcab-2260-479d-9ef6-dfb92d4f6061, rule.108.1.2026-09-25, decision.Lightning-Bolt.0.6, case.pvo-LEB-Lightning-Bolt, case.rv-Lightning-Bolt, diff.printing.b5d3dcab-2260-479d-9ef6-dfb92d4f6061

rows.question: My Limited Edition Alpha copy of False Orders reads "You decide whether and how one defending creature blocks, though you can't make a choice the defender couldn't legally make. Play after defender has chosen defense but before damage is dealt.". What does the card actually do now?
rows.answer:
Question type: printedVsOracle

Verdict: Your Alpha copy's wording has been completely replaced; the card is now an instant that, during the declare blockers step, removes a target creature the defending player controls from combat, unblocks anything that had become blocked by only it, and lets you have it block an attacking creature of your choice.

Missing: None — the current Oracle text, the Alpha printed text, and the CR rule that decides precedence were all retrieved, along with a decision document for this exact card.

Why: The Alpha text tells you to dictate a defender's blocking decision, which is a different mechanic from what Oracle now says. The decision document for this card characterizes the change as a different mechanic: the printed card dictates a defender's blocks, while Oracle removes a creature from combat and may have it block, which unblocks what it was blocking. The one ruling on file adds that triggered abilities that fired because the creature was declared as a blocker still happen even after it is removed. Note that the retrieved decision document is a model-assisted draft that has not been confirmed by a human, so treat it as a review artifact rather than a human-verified ruling.

Governing authority: Current Oracle text, under CR 108.1, which directs you to use the Oracle card reference when determining a card's wording. Oracle supersedes the printed Alpha wording.

Quote [Oracle text, complete]:
"Cast this spell only during the declare blockers step.
Remove target creature defending player controls from combat. Creatures it was blocking that had become blocked by only that creature this combat become unblocked. You may have it block an attacking creature of your choice."

Quote [Limited Edition Alpha printed text, complete]: "You decide whether and how one defending creature blocks, though you can't make a choice the defender couldn't legally make. Play after defender has chosen defense but before damage is dealt."

Quote [Ruling, 2004-10-04, complete]: "If a creature is removed from being a blocker of a given attacker, any triggered abilities that would have happened because it was declared as a blocker still happen."

Quote [CR 108.1, complete]: "Use the Oracle card reference when determining a card's wording. A card's Oracle text can be found using the Gatherer card database at Gatherer.Wizards.com."

Rules: 108.1

Conflict: The Alpha printed wording (you choose a defender's blocks) and the current Oracle wording (remove a creature from combat and optionally re-block) describe different mechanics. The Oracle wording wins under CR 108.1.

Sources: card.38c5c952-8153-4d98-89b5-a75260383345, decision.False-Orders.0.083, rule.108.1.2026-09-25, printing.7eb71ac4-796d-4011-9002-1129bc09c284

rows.question: My Unlimited Edition copy of Word of Command reads "You may look at opponent's hand and choose any card opponent can legally play using mana from his or her mana pool or lands. Opponent must play this card immediately; you make all the decisions it calls for. This spell may not be countered after you have looked at opponent's hand.". What does the card actually do now?
rows.answer:
Question type: printedVsOracle

Verdict: Your Unlimited Edition printing is superseded — current Oracle text makes Word of Command an effect that has you look at target opponent's hand, choose a card, gain control of that player while the spell resolves, and have them play that card if able, with restricted use of mana abilities; the printed "may not be countered" clause is gone.

Missing: None

Why: Under CR 108.1 you play the card using its Oracle wording, not the wording in your hand, and the reviewed decision document for this exact card (decision.Word-of-Command.0.257) confirms that Oracle governs and describes the same two changes: the printed uncounterable clause was removed entirely, and control of the player replaced the printed "you make all the decisions it calls for." The Oracle text also adds mana-ability restrictions (only mana abilities of lands that player controls, and only producing mana to activate other mana abilities of lands they control and/or to play the chosen card) that appear nowhere on the printed card. Two caveats on the evidence: that decision's claim list is empty and its confirmedByHuman field is unset (reviewedBy "joshua", reviewed 2026-09-19), so the resolution line itself is the reviewed authority; and the card's rulings entries explain the practical consequences (you order them to play the card if possible, you may command a land play, and opponents may still counter the spell you force them to cast, but not Word of Command after you look).

Governing authority: Current Oracle text, under CR 108.1 ("Use the Oracle card reference when determining a card's wording"), with CR 101.1 supplying card-over-rules precedence.

Quote (current Oracle text, card.e8ad3a77-b293-4d69-b080-27ca9f95d443, currentAsOf 2026-09-18): "Look at target opponent's hand and choose a card from it. You control that player until Word of Command finishes resolving. The player plays that card if able. While doing so, the player can activate mana abilities only if they're from lands that player controls and only if mana they produce is spent to activate other mana abilities of lands the player controls and/or to play that card. If the chosen card is cast as a spell, you control the player while that spell is resolving."

Quote (printed text, Unlimited Edition, printing.239c8547-207b-41d1-a2be-8825bfc6ef7f): "You may look at opponent's hand and choose any card opponent can legally play using mana from his or her mana pool or lands. Opponent must play this card immediately; you make all the decisions it calls for. This spell may not be countered after you have looked at opponent's hand."

Quote (CR 108.1, rule.108.1.2026-09-25): "Use the Oracle card reference when determining a card's wording. A card's Oracle text can be found using the Gatherer card database at Gatherer.Wizards.com."

Quote (CR 101.1, rule.101.1.2026-09-25): "Whenever a card's text directly contradicts these rules, the card takes precedence. The card overrides only the rule that applies to that specific situation. The only exception is that a player can concede the game at any time (see rule 104.3a)."

Quote (glossary, Oracle): "The reference that contains the up-to-date wordings (in English) for all tournament-legal cards. A card's Oracle text can be found using the Gatherer card database at Gatherer.Wizards.com. See rule 108.1."

Quote (ruling, 2011-01-01): "Your opponent can't counter the Word of Command after letting you look at their hand, but they can attempt to counter the spell you force them to cast."

Rules: 108.1, 101.1

Conflict: The printed card text ("This spell may not be countered after you have looked at opponent's hand"; "you make all the decisions it calls for") conflicts with the Oracle text, which deletes the anti-counter clause and replaces decision-making with controlling the player — Oracle wins under CR 108.1. All three printings I retrieved (Alpha, Beta, Unlimited) carry the identical printed text, and all three are flagged reviewState "functional" at similarity 0.257 in the textDifference records.

Sources: card.e8ad3a77-b293-4d69-b080-27ca9f95d443, printing.239c8547-207b-41d1-a2be-8825bfc6ef7f, printing.7d37b529-8a41-4177-abef-614f363e69d1, printing.96c21429-98d3-416b-be00-6aa9c4c5a006, decision.Word-of-Command.0.257, rule.108.1.2026-09-25, rule.101.1.2026-09-25, glossary.Oracle, diff.printing.239c8547-207b-41d1-a2be-8825bfc6ef7f, diff.printing.7d37b529-8a41-4177-abef-614f363e69d1, diff.printing.96c21429-98d3-416b-be00-6aa9c4c5a006

rows.question: My Fourth Edition copy of Mana Vault reads "Mana Vault does not untap during your untap phase. If it remains tapped during your upkeep, Mana Vault deals 1 damage to you. {4}: Untap Mana Vault. Use this ability only during your upkeep. ocT: Add three colorless mana to your mana pool. Play these additions as interrupts.". What does the card actually do now?
rows.answer:
Question type: printedVsOracle

Verdict: Your Fourth Edition Mana Vault behaves exactly as its current Oracle text reads — it skips your untap step, untaps only if you pay {4} as a triggered ability at the beginning of your upkeep, deals 1 damage to you at the beginning of your draw step while tapped, and taps for {C}{C}{C} — and the Fourth Edition wording it was printed with no longer applies.

Missing: None. (Only caveat: the three card-specific decision documents for Mana Vault in this corpus are model-assisted drafts with confirmedByHuman false; the reviewed authority here is the verified printedVsOracle case for this printing plus Oracle text and CR 108.1.)

Why: Current Oracle text, not the printing, defines what a card does, and CR 108.1 directs you to the Oracle reference for a card's wording. Three things changed on this card: the paid untap moved from an activated ability you chose to use during your upkeep into a triggered ability that triggers at the beginning of your upkeep and asks whether you pay {4}; the 1 damage moved from occurring while it "remains tapped during your upkeep" to the beginning of your draw step; and the mana ability is written with the {C} symbol, with the printed "play these additions as interrupts" instruction having no counterpart in the Oracle text at all. The corpus records this Fourth Edition printing as a functional difference (textDifference reviewState "functional", similarity 0.319), meaning the changes affect how the card plays, not just phrasing.

Governing authority: Current Oracle text for Mana Vault (currentAsOf 2026-09-18), under CR 108.1, which says to use the Oracle card reference to determine a card's wording; Oracle overrides the Fourth Edition printing's text.

Quote [Current Oracle text, Mana Vault]: This artifact doesn't untap during your untap step.
At the beginning of your upkeep, you may pay {4}. If you do, untap this artifact.
At the beginning of your draw step, if this artifact is tapped, it deals 1 damage to you.
{T}: Add {C}{C}{C}.

Quote [Printed text, Fourth Edition (4ED) Mana Vault]: Mana Vault does not untap during your untap phase. If it remains tapped during your upkeep, Mana Vault deals 1 damage to you.
{4}: Untap Mana Vault. Use this ability only during your upkeep.
ocT: Add three colorless mana to your mana pool. Play these additions as interrupts.

Quote [Comprehensive Rules 108.1]: Use the Oracle card reference when determining a card's wording. A card's Oracle text can be found using the Gatherer card database at Gatherer.Wizards.com.

Quote [Comprehensive Rules 101.1]: Whenever a card's text directly contradicts these rules, the card takes precedence. The card overrides only the rule that applies to that specific situation. The only exception is that a player can concede the game at any time (see rule 104.3a).

Rules: 108.1, 101.1

Conflict: The Fourth Edition printed text and the current Oracle text disagree on when the damage is dealt (upkeep vs. draw step), on how the {4} untap is initiated (an activated ability used only during your upkeep vs. a triggered ability at the beginning of your upkeep), and on the mana-ability templating ("play these additions as interrupts" vs. "{T}: Add {C}{C}{C}"). Under CR 108.1 the Oracle text wins, and the corpus marks this printing's difference as functional rather than cosmetic; no rule conflict exists between 108.1 and 101.1 here, since 101.1 addresses card text overriding the general rules and neither source contradicts 108.1.

Sources: card.736892cb-a34b-4bb9-b56c-e26e3db207a2, printing.3be9942c-89b3-422f-bb9d-b55f51a22a37, diff.printing.3be9942c-89b3-422f-bb9d-b55f51a22a37, rule.108.1.2026-09-25, rule.101.1.2026-09-25, decision.Mana-Vault.0.319, case.pvo-4ED-Mana-Vault

rows.question: My Tempest copy of Mogg Fanatic reads "Sacrifice Mogg Fanatic: Mogg Fanatic deals 1 damage to target creature or player.". What does the card actually do now?
rows.answer:
Question type: printedVsOracle

Verdict: Under current Oracle text the card reads "Sacrifice this creature: It deals 1 damage to any target," so the ability can now damage a planeswalker or battle as well as a creature or player.

Missing: None

Why: A verified adjudication case exists for this exact question and directs that the current Oracle text governs and that the Tempest printing must be named as the one it overrules. The Oracle text differs from your Tempest copy only in self-reference phrasing ("this creature" / "It" instead of the card's name) and in the targeting scope of the damage. That second change is the functional one: "target creature or player" is narrower than "any target," which the glossary defines as also including planeswalkers and battles. A text-difference record flags the printing as a functional difference (similarity 0.5).

Governing authority: Current Oracle text under CR 108.1 ("Use the Oracle card reference when determining a card's wording"), which supersedes the Tempest printed wording; targeting scope confirmed by the glossary entry for "Any Target."

Quote [Oracle text, current as of 2026-09-18]: Sacrifice this creature: It deals 1 damage to any target.
Quote [Tempest printing, TMP #190, released 1997-10-14]: Sacrifice Mogg Fanatic: Mogg Fanatic deals 1 damage to target creature or player.
Quote [CR 108.1, CR 2026-09-25]: Use the Oracle card reference when determining a card's wording. A card's Oracle text can be found using the Gatherer card database at Gatherer.Wizards.com.
Quote [glossary "Any Target"]: A spell or ability may require "any target." "Any target" is the same as "target creature, player, planeswalker, or battle." See rule 115.4.
Quote [verified adjudication case, case.pvo-TMP-Mogg-Fanatic]: Current Oracle text governs under CR 108.1: "Sacrifice this creature: It deals 1 damage to any target." The answer must reproduce this text completely and name the printing it overrules.
Quote [reviewed decision, decision.Mogg-Fanatic.0.5]: Oracle governs under CR 108.1. "Target creature or player" became "any target", adding planeswalkers and battles.
Quote [card ruling, published 2016-06-08]: Once Mogg Fanatic has dealt and been dealt combat damage, it's too late to activate its ability before it's destroyed.

Rules: 108.1 (retrieved verbatim). Note: rule 115.4 appears only as a cross-reference inside the "Any Target" glossary entry; I did not retrieve the text of 115.4, so I do not quote or apply it.

Conflict: None material. The verified adjudication case and the model-assisted decision document agree; the decision document is unconfirmed (reviewMethod "model-assisted", confirmedByHuman false), so the verified adjudication case is the stronger authority, and its expected verdict does not itself state the planeswalker/battle detail — that detail comes from the glossary definition of "Any Target."

Sources: card.7efd5d62-6da2-428a-98e3-5b842f668656, printing.ca2ecfd4-c874-4468-8601-87aa110d5a00, diff.printing.ca2ecfd4-c874-4468-8601-87aa110d5a00, rule.108.1.2026-09-25, glossary.Any-Target, case.pvo-TMP-Mogg-Fanatic, decision.Mogg-Fanatic.0.5

rows.question: Can Mogg Fanatic assign combat damage, sacrifice itself in response, and still deal that combat damage?
rows.answer:
Question type: historical
Verdict: No — under the current rules Mogg Fanatic cannot assign combat damage, then be sacrificed in response, and still deal that combat damage; that line played only before the Magic 2010 rules change in July 2009, when combat damage used the stack.
Missing: The corpus contains no 2009 Comprehensive Rules text and no authority document for the Magic 2010 rules change, so the historical half of the answer ("combat damage used the stack, so this worked") rests only on the verified case case.rv-Mogg-Fanatic and its companion cases, not on a retrieved rules document.
Why: Under the current rules, combat damage is assigned and dealt as turn-based actions that don't use the stack, and no player receives priority between assignment and dealing, so there is no window in which to activate the sacrifice ability "in response." The ability itself is unchanged, which is why the case is framed as a rules-version change rather than a card change. The old play worked because damage was assigned and then went on the stack, letting the Fanatic be sacrificed after damage was assigned but before it resolved.
Governing authority: Current Comprehensive Rules 510.1 and 510.2 (CR 2026-09-25), under the verified rules-version adjudication case case.rv-Mogg-Fanatic; the card identity and ability text come from the Oracle entry for Mogg Fanatic under CR 108.1.
Quote [Oracle text — Mogg Fanatic]: Sacrifice this creature: It deals 1 damage to any target.
Quote [Ruling, 2016-06-08]: Once Mogg Fanatic has dealt and been dealt combat damage, it's too late to activate its ability before it's destroyed.
Quote [CR 510.1, CR 2026-09-25]: First, the active player announces how each attacking creature assigns its combat damage, then the defending player announces how each blocking creature assigns its combat damage. This turn-based action doesn't use the stack. A player assigns a creature's combat damage according to the following rules:
Quote [CR 510.2, CR 2026-09-25]: Second, all combat damage that's been assigned is dealt simultaneously. This turn-based action doesn't use the stack. No player has the chance to cast spells or activate abilities between the time combat damage is assigned and the time it's dealt.
Quote [case.rv-Mogg-Fanatic, expected verdict]: No, not under the current rules. Before the Magic 2010 rules change in July 2009 combat damage used the stack, so this worked. The activated ability relevant to this interaction did not materially change; the rules governing combat damage did.
Quote [case.rv-Nantuko-Husk, expected verdict]: Yes, before the Magic 2010 rules change in July 2009. Not since. Wizards named this exact interaction as one of the confusing cases the change removed. The last chance to sacrifice is now the declare blockers step.
Rules: 510.1, 510.2, 108.1
Conflict: The printed Tempest text ("Sacrifice Mogg Fanatic: Mogg Fanatic deals 1 damage to target creature or player.") differs from the Oracle text's "any target," but that difference is not what decides this question; CR 108.1 makes Oracle govern the wording, and CR 510.1–510.2 decide the timing. No source in the corpus contradicts the current-rules answer.

rows.question: If I tap for more mana than I spend on Fireball, do I take damage at the end of the phase?

Verdict: No — unspent mana no longer causes damage; mana burn was eliminated by the Magic 2010 rules change in July 2009, so surplus mana from tapping for Fireball simply empties from your mana pool.

Two gaps worth flagging: the case lists no required rule numbers, and the corpus contains no Comprehensive Rules paragraph on mana emptying/burn — the glossary entry for "Mana Pool" only cross-references rule 106.4, whose text was not retrieved. The corpus's own label for this question is "rulesVersion" (a category outside my five output types); I filed it as historical because the answer turns on which rules version applies.

rows.question: When Word of Command resolves, who controls the opponent, and for how long?
rows.answer:
Question type: currentWording
Verdict: You control the targeted opponent until Word of Command finishes resolving, and if the chosen card is cast as a spell, you also control that player while that spell is resolving.
Missing: None
Why: The card's complete current Oracle text states exactly who controls the player and for how long, and CR 108.1 makes that Oracle wording the authoritative text. A verified adjudication case matching this exact question reaches the same result. The duration is bounded: control ends when the spell finishes resolving, except that it resumes for the resolution of the spell the chosen card becomes.
Governing authority: Current Oracle text of Word of Command, under CR 108.1 ("Use the Oracle card reference when determining a card's wording").
Quote Oracle text (complete): "Look at target opponent's hand and choose a card from it. You control that player until Word of Command finishes resolving. The player plays that card if able. While doing so, the player can activate mana abilities only if they're from lands that player controls and only if mana they produce is spent to activate other mana abilities of lands the player controls and/or to play that card. If the chosen card is cast as a spell, you control the player while that spell is resolving."
Quote Ruling (2011-01-01): "During the resolution of this spell, that player plays the chosen card."
Quote Ruling (2004-10-04): "To \"play a card\" is to either cast a spell or to put a land onto the battlefield using the main phase special action."
Quote Ruling (2011-01-01): "You control the player while this spell is resolving, which means you get to see anything they can see. If that player is required to search their library as part of playing the card or as part of its resolution if it's cast as a spell, then you can see the cards in that player's library as well."
Quote Ruling (2016-07-13): "While controlling another player, you can see all cards in the game that player can see. This includes cards in that player's hand, face-down cards that player controls, and any cards in that player's library the player may look at."
Quote supporting case verdict (case.rv-Word-of-Command, verified): "You control that player until Word of Command finishes resolving, and if the chosen card is cast as a spell you control the player while that spell is resolving too. The complete current Oracle text must be quoted, including the mana-ability restrictions, which appear nowhere on the Alpha printing."
Quote CR 108.1: "Use the Oracle card reference when determining a card's wording. A card's Oracle text can be found using the Gatherer card database at Gatherer.Wizards.com."
Rules: 108.1
Conflict: None for the current behavior; the Oracle text is self-consistent on duration. (The only tension in the sources is historical — the reviewed decision decision.Word-of-Command.0.257 notes the printed uncounterable clause was removed and "you make all the decisions it calls for" was replaced by control of the player — but that is a printed-vs-Oracle matter, not a conflict within current wording.)
Sources: card.e8ad3a77-b293-4d69-b080-27ca9f95d443, case.rv-Word-of-Command, decision.Word-of-Command.0.257, rule.108.1.2026-09-25

rows.question: Is Chaos Orb's physical flip requirement still part of its Oracle text?
rows.answer:
Question type: currentWording
Verdict: Yes — the physical flip requirement is still part of Chaos Orb's current Oracle text; the wording has been retemplated, not removed.
Missing: None
Why: Chaos Orb's current Oracle text still instructs you to flip the artifact onto the battlefield from a height of at least one foot, and still conditions the destruction on it turning over completely at least once during the flip, so the physical act is retained. What changed is the templating: Oracle adds {T} to the activation cost, checks that the artifact is on the battlefield, and destroys only nontoken permanents. A verified, human-reviewed decision document for this exact question agrees, and CR 108.1 makes Oracle text the controlling wording.
Governing authority: Current Oracle text, under CR 108.1 (Oracle card reference determines a card's wording).
Quote [Current Oracle text — Chaos Orb, card.edb455f4-8dc9-4b7c-b25c-cb51b7dfbb41, current as of 2026-09-18]: "{1}, {T}: If this artifact is on the battlefield, flip it onto the battlefield from a height of at least one foot. If this artifact turns over completely at least once during the flip, destroy all nontoken permanents it touches. Then destroy this artifact."
Quote [CR 108.1, rule.108.1.2026-09-25]: "Use the Oracle card reference when determining a card's wording. A card's Oracle text can be found using the Gatherer card database at Gatherer.Wizards.com."
Quote [Ruling, Chaos Orb, 2004-10-04]: "It must flip 360 degrees (that's what \"flip\" means). And this flip must be in the air and not in your hand."
Quote [Reviewed decision, case.rv-Chaos-Orb, expectedVerdict]: "Yes. Current Oracle text still requires flipping the card onto the battlefield from a height of at least one foot, and it must turn over completely at least once. The wording was retemplated but the physical requirement remains."
Quote [Printed text, Limited Edition Alpha/Beta and Unlimited Edition]: "{1}: Flip Chaos Orb onto the playing area from a height of at least one foot. Chaos Orb must turn completely over at least once or it is discarded with no effect. When Chaos Orb lands, any cards in play that it touches are destroyed, as is Chaos Orb."
Rules: 108.1
Conflict: Two decision documents exist for Chaos Orb. The verified, human-reviewed adjudication case (case.rv-Chaos-Orb.346 question) answers this exact question "Yes", while decision.Chaos-Orb.0.346 is a model-assisted, unconfirmed draft answering a different (printedVsOracle) question about the {T} cost and token exclusion. The verified adjudication case is preferred. Separately, the 2019-01-27 ruling supplies an entirely different, format-specific text for Chaos Orb in the Old School format; that is an alternate text for that format, not the Oracle wording, so it does not override the Oracle text.

rows.question: The printed card just says 'Bands'. What does the card actually do, and did its function change?
rows.answer:
Question type: printedVsOracle

Verdict: The Alpha printing's "Bands" is shorthand for the banding keyword ability, which the current Oracle text spells out in full; the function is the same, Banding, so it did not change.

Missing: None.

Why: A reviewed case for this exact question exists and is marked verified, and it states that the printed text is shorthand for banding which Oracle spells out in full, and that the function did not change. The corpus independently flags the Alpha, Beta, Unlimited, Fourth and Fifth Edition printings with a very low measured text similarity of 0.025, yet marks every one of those differences "nonfunctional". Under CR 108.1 the Oracle text is what governs a card's wording, so the one-word printing is read as the full keyword ability. One caveat: the corpus's ruleParagraph set contains 108.1, 101.1, 510.1, 510.2, 600-series and 700-series paragraphs but not rule 702.22 itself, so the mechanical detail below comes from the Oracle reminder text and the card's official rulings rather than from the rule 702.22 text.

Governing authority: Current Oracle text, under CR 108.1 ("Use the Oracle card reference when determining a card's wording"), as applied by the verified reviewed case case.rv-Benalish-Hero.

Quote [printed text, Limited Edition Alpha, collector #4]: Bands

Quote [current Oracle text, Benalish Hero]: Banding (Any creatures with banding, and up to one without, can attack in a band. Bands are blocked as a group. If any creatures with banding you control are blocking or being blocked by a creature, you divide that creature's combat damage, not its controller, among any of the creatures it's being blocked by or is blocking.)

Quote [CR 108.1]: Use the Oracle card reference when determining a card's wording. A card's Oracle text can be found using the Gatherer card database at Gatherer.Wizards.com.

Quote [CR 101.1]: Whenever a card's text directly contradicts these rules, the card takes precedence. The card overrides only the rule that applies to that specific situation. The only exception is that a player can concede the game at any time (see rule 104.3a).

Quote [ruling, 2008-10-01]: If a creature with banding attacks, it can team up with any number of other attacking creatures with banding (and up to one nonbanding creature) and attack as a unit called a "band." The band can be blocked by any creature that could block a single creature in the band. Blocking any creature in a band blocks the entire band. If a creature with banding is blocked, the attacking player chooses how the blockers' damage is assigned.

Quote [glossary, Banding, "Bands with Other"]: Banding is a keyword ability that modifies the rules for declaring attackers and assigning combat damage. "Bands with other" is a specialized version of the ability. See rule 702.22, "Banding."

Quote [reviewed case, case.rv-Benalish-Hero, expected verdict]: The printed text is shorthand for banding, which the current Oracle text spells out in full. Measured text similarity is 0.025 but the function did not change. Oracle governs under CR 108.1.

Rules: 108.1, 101.1, 510.1, 510.2

Conflict: The Alpha/Beta/Unlimited printed wording ("Bands") conflicts with the current Oracle wording (the full banding text). Oracle wins under CR 108.1, and because the printing is shorthand for the same keyword, the conflict is textual only — the corpus records it as "nonfunctional" at similarity 0.025.

Sources: case.rv-Benalish-Hero, case.pvo-LEA-Benalish-Hero, card.4c81cfb7-8765-4e28-ae33-4287fa9a86cc, printing.11600105-56c6-4073-a4a6-8469030b39c9, printing.32dcd608-ef94-4047-841d-5c3471375d5d, printing.9404e779-2065-4c4f-95d1-6997c7fea156, printing.f62c68d0-9b1e-4abe-991d-a645effeb676, printing.fd204832-5f3b-4213-9c06-b89a296a9d47, diff.printing.11600105-56c6-4073-a4a6-8469030b39c9, diff.printing.32dcd608-ef94-4047-841d-5c3471375d5d, diff.printing.9404e779-2065-4c4f-95d1-6997c7fea156, diff.printing.f62c68d0-9b1e-4abe-991d-a645effeb676, diff.printing.fd204832-5f3b-4213-9c06-b89a296a9d47, rule.108.1.2026-09-25, rule.108.1.2026-08-07, rule.101.1.2026-09-25, rule.101.1.2026-08-07, rule.510.1.2026-09-25, rule.510.2.2026-09-25, glossary.Banding---Bands-with-Other-

rows.question: My Alpha Lightning Bolt says 'one target'. Can I still point it at a planeswalker?
rows.answer:
Question type: printedVsOracle

Verdict: Yes — current Oracle text governs, and "any target" includes planeswalkers, so your Alpha Lightning Bolt can be pointed at a planeswalker.

Missing: The full text of CR 115.4 was not retrieved; ruleParagraph documents exist only for 100.2, 100.4, 101.1, 108.1, 510.1, 510.2, 608.2 and 700.2, so the "any target" enumeration is cited here from the glossary term that references 115.4, not from the rule paragraph itself.

Why: Your Alpha printing says "one target", but a card's wording for play is the Oracle text, not the printing in your hand. Oracle reads "any target", which the glossary defines as target creature, player, planeswalker, or battle. So the spell's reach now includes planeswalkers even though the printed card never said so — the general rules for card wording prefer Oracle over the physical printing.

Governing authority: Current Oracle text, under CR 108.1 ("Use the Oracle card reference when determining a card's wording").

Quote [Oracle text — card.4457ed35, complete]: Lightning Bolt deals 3 damage to any target.

Quote [Printed text — Limited Edition Alpha (LEA 161), complete]: Lightning Bolt does 3 damage to one target.

Quote [CR 108.1 — rule.108.1.2026-09-25, complete]: Use the Oracle card reference when determining a card's wording. A card's Oracle text can be found using the Gatherer card database at Gatherer.Wizards.com.

Quote [Glossary "Any Target" — complete]: A spell or ability may require "any target." "Any target" is the same as "target creature, player, planeswalker, or battle." See rule 115.4.

Quote [Reviewed decision resolution — decision.Lightning-Bolt.0.6, complete]: Oracle governs under CR 108.1. "One target" became "any target", adding planeswalkers and battles. Similarity is 0.600, the high end of the set, yet the function changed.

Rules: 108.1

Conflict: The Alpha printed text ("one target") disagrees with the current Oracle text ("any target"). Oracle wins under CR 108.1. The textDifference record for the Alpha printing confirms this divergence is classified "functional" at similarity 0.600 — high textual similarity, changed function.

Sources: card.4457ed35-7c10-48c8-9776-456485fdf070, printing.d573ef03-4730-45aa-93dd-e45ac1dbaf4a, diff.printing.d573ef03-4730-45aa-93dd-e45ac1dbaf4a, rule.108.1.2026-09-25, glossary.Any-Target, glossary.Planeswalker, decision.Lightning-Bolt.0.6, case.rv-Lightning-Bolt
